newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end lower; small-caps hammered.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end lower; small-caps hammered.

text.p: Malaysian stocks closed broadly lower on heavy volumes, with Second Board shares the worst hit sector after spectacular recent gains.
The Second Board index sank 24.86 points at 600.55 or 3.97 percent. The Composite Index of 100 leading stocks was down 0.50 points at 1128.81.

"It's a temporary set-back," said Mohamad Zamri, an institutional dealer at brokers K & N Kenanga. "The falls may be due to fears about restrictions over margin facilities for Second Board stocks," said Zamri.
TRI was up 50 cents to 6.80 ringgit on heavy trading.

"There have been rumours of some local broking houses imposing restrictions like demanding a certain percentage of cash for share transactions up front," said an institutional dealer at a Singapore-based broking house.
"There was even talk of the authorities imposing restrictions to curb speculation," he added.
The dealer said that he had seen investors switching into main board stocks.
At the close, 378 million shares were traded, valued at 3.2 billion ringgit. Losers outnumbered gainers 346 to 250 while 121 stocks were unchanged.
